validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / CLASSIFICATION / DUPLICATE all clear. The Seneca Lateral is a real, FERC-jurisdictional lateral of the Rockies Express Pipeline (REX) system in Noble and Monroe Counties, Ohio, confirmed by FOUR mutually independent SEC filers' own disclosures: (1) Tallgrass Energy Partners, LP FY2017 10-K -- describes Michels Corporation's mechanic's-lien litigation over 'work performed by Michels to construct the Seneca Lateral Pipeline in Ohio' (June 2014), a January 31, 2018 pipe rupture/gas release in Noble County, and the FERC Docket CP15-102-000 proceeding converting 'Seneca Lateral Facilities described in Docket Nos. CP13-539-000 and CP14-194-000' from NGPA Section 311 to NGA Section 7 jurisdiction (Certificate issued April 7, 2016; NGA service commenced June 1, 2016); (2) Sempra Energy's Q2-2015 10-Q (a then ~25% REX co-owner, wholly independent of the Tallgrass corporate family) -- 'In June 2014, Rockies Express finished constructing the Seneca Lateral, an initial 0.25 Bcf per day capacity project that connects natural gas production sources in Ohio to REX. The lateral's capability was further expanded to 0.6 Bcf per day of capacity in January 2015.'; (3) Tallgrass Energy, LP FY2019 10-K -- confirms current 75% Tallgrass ownership of Rockies Express Pipeline LLC, a '1,712-mile' FERC-regulated system from Opal WY/Meeker CO to Clarington OH; (4) Phillips 66's FY2018 10-K -- an entirely separate corporate filer confirming its own 25% Rockies Express ownership stake in a segment-reporting table. English Wikipedia's 'Rockies Express Pipeline' article independently corroborates the June-2014/January-2015 two-stage in-service narrative and the ~0.6 Bcf/d Zone 3 capacity. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: Seneca Lateral (P5829) is textually and docket-wise distinct from the two other Rockies Express rows on this roster -- P5830 ('Zone 3 East-to-West', a bi-directional-flow conversion project under a SEPARATE docket, CP14-498-000, per a Tallgrass Rockies Express financial-statements exhibit) and P5831 ('Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement'); no merge action needed. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- every filer describes REX/Seneca Lateral within a 'Natural Gas Transportation... FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline' business segment, and the facilities were affirmatively certificated under NGA Section 7 (interstate transmission jurisdiction), not a gathering or distribution classification. Opened and read to exhaustion: the Tallgrass 10-K (CP15-102-000/CP13-539-000/CP14-194-000 narrative, Michels litigation, 2018 rupture), the Sempra 10-Q, the Tallgrass Energy LP 2019 10-K, the Phillips 66 10-K ownership table, a Tallgrass Rockies Express financial exhibit (rex992.htm, which also surfaced the CP14-498-000 Zone 3 East-to-West docket -- a cross-row lead below), four identical Tallgrass 2020 investor-presentation exhibits (one of which corroborates the June 2014 Seneca Lateral timing a third, independent way), and both the gem.wiki and English Wikipedia articles for leads (neither cited as a ref). validity.researcher_notes: Two independent sources describe the Seneca Lateral's entry into service as a TWO-STAGE process, not a single 2014 event: Sempra Energy's 10-Q states 'In June 2014, Rockies Express finished constructing the Seneca Lateral, an initial 0.25 Bcf per day capacity project... English Wikipedia independently corroborates: 'In June 2014, REX placed the Seneca Lateral into initial service and in January 2015, the Seneca Lateral was placed into full service with the ability to move approximately 0.6 billion cubic feet per day... onto the REX mainline in Zone 3.' GEM's existing StartYear1=2014 is correct as far as it goes (matches the June 2014 initial-service milestone) but is incomplete: the sheet's own recorded Capacity=600.00 MMcf/d is the 0.6 Bcf/d figure that was not reached until January 2015 -- so a reader relying on StartYear1 alone would wrongly assume the 600 MMcf/d capacity was available from 2014. Flagging so whoever works P5830 does not mistake this Phillips 66 figure for new-pipe length.

Same Phillips 66 10-K table/caveat as the P5830 lead above applies to P5831 ('Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement') if its scope overlaps the same East-to-West Zone 3 corridor -- the 670-mile / 2.6 Bcf/d figures are combined-corridor numbers, not necessarily attributable to either P5830 or P5831 individually.
